why_this_record_exists: A zero exit from `git push` is not evidence of publication. Reproduced in this estate: two lanes committed on the shared /workspace checkout's detached HEAD, so their branch refs never advanced, and `git push -u origin <branch>` then pushed the stale ref while printing 'Everything up-to-date' and exiting 0. Both lanes would have reported success against an effectively empty branch.

A read-back that merely names a commit is also not enough. A fabricated read-back naming a nonexistent commit once passed a producer's own verifier here. So this record does not rest on asserting a SHA: it re-derives file hashes from bytes fetched back out of the remote by a process that never saw the working tree.

method.step_2: git checkout cursor/oe-w5-agentic-office-696d in the fresh clone
method.step_3: sha256 every delivered file in the fresh clone and compare against the same path in the working tree
method.independence_note: The clone is a separate directory populated only from the remote. It shares no object store, no index and no working tree with /tmp/oe-w5. The comparison is therefore between bytes GitHub served and bytes this lane wrote, not between a file and itself.

observation_1_publication_is_real.what_this_rules_out: The exit-zero-on-a-stale-ref failure. A fresh clone reached this commit from the remote, so the ref genuinely advanced rather than the push silently no-opping.

observation_2_bytes_survive_the_round_tr.scope: Every file delivered as of cdb2d8f7: the launch guide, all of w5-agentic-office/, and the lane's raw receipts.

why_no_per_file_hash_list_is_duplicated_.statement: Per-file hashes live in MANIFEST.json and are deliberately not copied into this record.
why_no_per_file_hash_list_is_duplicated_.reason: This record is written before the final commit, so any hash list embedded in it goes stale the moment a covered file is amended — and a stale hash list that still reads as a verification is worse than none. The guide was in fact amended after cdb2d8f7 to add the manifest-check command, which is exactly the case that would have rotted a copied list.
why_no_per_file_hash_list_is_duplicated_.single_authority: MANIFEST.json holds path, size_bytes and sha256 for every delivered file, plus entry_count and a bundle_sha256 a third party recomputes independently.

the_closing_check_a_reviewer_should_run.statement: This record and MANIFEST.json cannot appear in a clone taken before the commit that carries them. The regress is closed by running the check against the final branch head, where every file including this one is present.
the_closing_check_a_reviewer_should_run.expected: PASS, with entry_count and bundle_sha256 recomputed from the remote's own bytes. That single command supersedes this record: it verifies every delivered file, including this one, from a clone that never saw the producing runtime.

what_this_record_does_not_establish: That the guide is correct. Publication and byte-integrity are not acceptance. Nothing here rises above DURABLE on the admission ladder.
That any claim inside the guide was independently validated. S-ACCEPT has not run against this bundle.
That the manifest's own bytes are verified by this record. The manifest is verified by the commit that carries it and by its own --check.
